requirements.requirement: Configure PostgreSQL streaming replication with node1 as writable primary and node2/node3 as read-only standbys
requirements.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both node2 (10.100.163.11) and node3 (10.100.163.12) in 'streaming' state with walreceiver connections. On both standbys, pg_is_in_recovery() returns true and an attempted INSERT fails with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction', directly confirming read-only standby behavior. Replication uses a dedicated 'replicator' role over scram-sha-256 with pg_hba.conf scoped to the cluster subnet, and pg_basebackup -R was used to bootstrap standby.signal/primary_conninfo on both replicas.

requirements.requirement: Changes committed on the primary should be visible on both standbys
requirements.summary: A row inserted on node1 ('streamed-row-2') appeared on both node2 and node3 within ~1 second via SELECT, with pg_last_wal_replay_lsn on each standby advancing to match the primary's LSN. This was independently re-confirmed after all three nodes were rebooted: a post-restart insert ('post-restart-row-3') on the primary was visible on both standbys moments later.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state on every managed node
requirements.summary: All three nodes were rebooted sequentially (node2, node3, node1) via backgrounded systemctl reboot with acks returned before disconnect. Each node shows a pre-restart boot_id, connection timeouts during the reboot window, and a distinct post-restart boot_id with fresh uptime, matching the fixed global before_prepare/after_executor snapshots (e.g. node1 deef5424->e45fe999, node2 cce73776->64af8f27, node3 4d842549->a5f590a0). After each reboot, postgresql was confirmed active, standbys showed correct recovery state with data intact, and the primary (rebooted last) showed pg_is_in_recovery()=f, both standbys reconnected streaming, and a fresh write replicated successfully.

overall_summary: Both material contract outcomes -- primary/standby topology with read-only enforcement, and replication of committed changes to both standbys -- are directly and repeatedly demonstrated, including after a full sequential reboot of all three nodes with preserved quorum and a working post-restart write test. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol is well-executed and cross-checked against the fixed global boot-identity snapshots. The main blemish is an operational hygiene lapse: a replication password partially leaked into the captured transcript via a failed redaction attempt, and a plaintext password file was left on disk on all nodes instead of being cleaned up.
limitations: The replication password fragment visible in cmd-7f9ec522c4e142fb's output constitutes a real secret exposure in evidence, though it is scoped to a lab/test cluster and low-risk in this context.

Node1's pre-restart baseline was captured at session start (cmd-a2036671826e477a/cmd-bc62b58a12dc496b) rather than immediately before its own reboot, but no intervening changes to node1's boot state occurred so this does not affect the restart-protocol assessment.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were clearly tied to the replication task or the restart protocol (package installs, firewalld rule for postgresql, wal_level/pg_hba edits, replicator role, pg_basebackup rebuild of standby data directories, sequential reboots). Two issues lower the score: (1) an attempted redaction of the replication password on node2 via sed (cmd-7f9ec522c4e142fb) failed and the immediately following unredacted 'cat /var/lib/pgsql/data/postgresql.auto.conf' printed a large fragment of the actual replication password into captured evidence -- a real secret-exposure incident in the transcript, contradicting the executor's claim that the password was 'never printed to the transcript except one accidental...dump' framed as contained; the exposure is present in evidence provided to this reviewer. (2) The plaintext replication password file /root/repl_pass.txt was left in place (chmod 600) on all three nodes rather than deleted after distribution -- an unnecessary residual secret, though access-restricted to root. A minor, low-impact epel-release install on node1 (cmd-db71888c6d4f49d7) was superfluous since postgresql-server was already available via appstream, but this is low severity and did not affect package health (post-executor package-health checks show no issues on any node).
